newsitem.title: FINLAND: Outokumpu stock falls as profit slumps.
newsitem.headline: Outokumpu stock falls as profit slumps.

text.p: Shares in Finnish metals and mining group Outokumpu Oy on Monday fell after it reported an 84 percent slump in profit for 1996 but saw some signs of gradual improvement.
Reporting profit before extraordinary items and tax at 229 million markka from 1.48 billion in 1995, Outokumpu proposed a 1.00 markka dividend against 1.80 for 1995.

The result was clearly below analysts' median forecast for the group at 298 million markka in a 150-395 million markka range, and its stock was marked down 3.00 markka or over three percent to 82.00 markka in quiet early Helsinki trade.
Outokumpu's net sales dipped to 16.55 billion markka from 16.95 billion a year ago, pressured by falling prices in stainless steel, ferrochrome and copper.
"The average market price of stainless steel was 34 percent lower than in 1995; the price of ferrochrome was 20 percent and that of copper 22 percent lower," Outokumpu said in a statement.

But stainless steel and copper prices hit bottom in August-September and ferrochrome in late 1996, it said; adding that an average five percent strengthening of the dollar against the markka had softened the blow on profitability.
"The Outokumpu group's outlook for 1997 has improved during the past few months although a great deal of uncertainty prevails," Outokumpu said.

"Market conditions are forecast to improve during 1997. The strength of the U.S. dollar will also improve conditions for profitability. Earnings in the early part of the year are nevertheless likely to remain modest," it said.
